title: The Problem of Replication
text:
Replication is the cornerstone of scientific research. When independent teams repeat an experiment and obtain the same results, confidence in the original findings grows considerably. Yet many published studies have never been replicated at all, partly because journals tend to favour novel discoveries over confirmatory work.

The consequences of this imbalance are significant. Researchers may build entire theories on results that later prove fragile, and policymakers may act on evidence that is less secure than it appears. Some scientists therefore advocate pre-registering study designs, which commits researchers to a method before data are collected.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what increases confidence in original findings?
options: Independent teams repeating the experiment and obtaining the same results
Researchers working entirely on their own
Experiments that last for many years

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what is pre-registering?
options: Publishing the data after a study has ended
Committing to a method before the data are collected

questions.text: What does the writer suggest about journals' editorial preferences?
options: They reward confirmatory work as much as novel discoveries
They prefer studies that are never published
They accept research only from policymakers

questions.text: Why might policymakers be misled by research, according to the passage?
options: Because the evidence may be less secure than it appears
Because scientists refuse to share their results

vocabulary.definition: the repetition of a study to check whether its results can be obtained again
the basic element on which something else depends
weak or likely to fail under pressure
intended to check or support an existing result

paragraph_translations: A replicação é a pedra angular da pesquisa científica. Quando equipes independentes repetem um experimento e obtêm os mesmos resultados, a confiança nas descobertas originais cresce consideravelmente. No entanto, muitos estudos publicados nunca foram replicados, em parte porque as revistas tendem a favorecer descobertas inéditas em vez de trabalhos confirmatórios.

As consequências desse desequilíbrio são significativas. Pesquisadores podem construir teorias inteiras com base em resultados que depois se mostram frágeis, e formuladores de políticas podem agir com base em evidências menos seguras do que parecem. Por isso, alguns cientistas defendem o pré-registro dos desenhos de estudo, que compromete os pesquisadores com um método antes da coleta dos dados.
